Profile fields:
  simulation_profile: SINGLE_TANK_LEVEL
  plant_equation: dh/dt=u+d
  state_unit: metre
  u_unit: metre/second
  safe_envelope: h in [0,10]
  disturbance_bound: abs(d)<=0.1
  actuator_bound: u in [-1,1]
  fallback_controller: u=+0.2 when h<=5 else -0.2
  sensor_error_bound: 0.05m
  sensor_age_bound: 0.10s
  monitor_period_bound: 0.10s
  handoff_delay_bound: 0.20s
  safety_margin: 0.05+1.1*(0.10+0.10+0.20)=0.49m
  switching_thresholds: measured h<=0.49 or h>=9.51
  takeover_recoverable_region(D,e): estimated level center in [1.1*D+e,10-1.1*D-e], D>=0 seconds, e>=0 metres; empty if lower>upper; actual initial uncertainty interval [h_hat-e,h_hat+e] must lie within [1.1*D,10-1.1*D]
  verification_receipt: dynamics,uncertainty,initial_conditions,step_size,solver,seed,fault_schedule,timings,trajectories,properties,loss_of_assurance
  switching_threshold_qualification: PROPOSED_ARITHMETIC_NOT_VALIDATED
  threshold_proof_obligation: sensor error sign, sampling phase, observation age, monitoring period, remaining handoff delay, actuator dynamics, primary/fallback command ordering, uncertainty interval propagation, numerical discretization error
Normative candidate invariants:
EH-18-001: The selected example is a dimensioned abstract tank-level simulation, not a deployment-ready physical safety case. Plant, primary controller, independently implemented fallback, switch, sensor and actuator each have exact versioned profiles and authenticated interfaces.
EH-18-002: Primary controller may choose any admitted u within [-1,1]. Worst outward speed is 1.1 m/s. Candidate margin 0.05+1.1*(0.10+0.10+0.20)=0.49m combines measurement error and worst observation age, monitoring phase and handoff delay. This arithmetic is a proposed bound, not validated safety evidence. A continuous-time/interval proof MUST cover error sign, arbitrary sampling phase, delay decomposition without missing or double-counting intervals, threshold comparison semantics, actuator dynamics/latency, competing-command order and numerical discretization error before qualifying switching thresholds.
EH-18-003: Fallback pushes inward at net speed at least 0.1m/s at either boundary under stated disturbance/actuator assumptions. This supports an invariant envelope only after timely successful handoff with valid state; it is not a guarantee under actuator failure or violated assumptions.
EH-18-004: Define takeover_recoverable_region(D,e) for remaining uncontrolled delay D>=0 seconds and level estimation uncertainty e>=0 metres. Estimated center h_hat must satisfy h_hat in [1.1D+e,10-1.1D-e]; equivalently the actual initial uncertainty interval [h_hat-e,h_hat+e] is contained in [1.1D,10-1.1D]. Reachability over delay expands it to [h_hat-e-1.1D,h_hat+e+1.1D], which must remain in [0,10]. An empty interval is nonrecoverable. [0,10] applies only to exact actual state at completed takeover with D=0 and the specified functioning fallback; it is not an unconditional delayed-handoff entry region. Initial stale observations use full remaining delay and estimation uncertainty.
EH-18-005: STPA identifies unsafe control actions at switching: missing/late switch, early return, conflicting controller commands, incorrect state transfer, stale sensor interpretation and unsafe shutdown. Each maps to a constraint, owner and test.
EH-18-006: Fallback independence includes control code, execution resources, authority/credentials, sensing and actuation failure assumptions, plus common-cause analysis; shared hardware is explicitly modeled, not silently independent.
EH-18-007: Authenticated minimal state transfer binds time, controller, epoch and integrity. Actuator rejects stale primary commands after switch epoch. Failed handoff retains explicit loss-of-assurance and qualified minimum-risk response.
EH-18-008: Test outside recoverable region and outside envelope. Choose minimum-risk response under a declared loss function/safety case, e.g. maximum inward control if actuator remains trustworthy; it cannot be described as guaranteed safe when reachability says otherwise.
EH-18-009: Return to primary requires root-cause closure, revalidation, fresh authorization, valid envelope and anti-chatter dwell/hysteresis conditions demonstrated compatible with immediate safety override.
EH-18-010: Simulation receipts record assumptions, parameter bounds, timing measurements, trajectories, solver discretization error and per-property results; no simulated result is invented by source-design acceptance.
FunctionContract REQUIREMENT PROFILE — machine binding UNRESOLVED:
operation: single-plant profile of contain_critical_continuity and resilience validation
preconditions: Pinned dynamics/uncertainty, validated timing/envelope region, independently qualified fallback and fresh authority.
postconditions: Handoff meets derived bound within assumptions or explicit assurance-loss/minimum-risk state; return requires fresh authorization.
failures: LATE_HANDOFF, STATE_UNTRUSTED, OUTSIDE_RECOVERABLE_REGION, ACTUATOR_UNTRUSTED, ASSURANCE_LOST; no false guarantee.

Failure/conformance test specifications:
TEST-EH-18-001: Sensor delay/error at allowed bounds, outward primary command and worst disturbance: switch before state exits envelope, verified by bounded dynamics analysis and numerical error accounting.
TEST-EH-18-002: Controller timeout and failed handoff: fence stale primary commands; record actual trajectory and loss of guarantee when delay budget exceeded.
TEST-EH-18-003: Disturbance above 0.1 or handoff delay above 0.20: assumptions invalidated and no PASS under original safety claim.
TEST-EH-18-004: Start inside [0,10] but outside delayed recoverable region: immediate appropriate response, no false recoverability claim.
TEST-EH-18-005: Start outside safe envelope: record violation; apply justified minimum-risk response, never claim historical safety.
TEST-EH-18-006: Stale authenticated transfer packet and delayed old primary actuator command: epoch/freshness rejection.
TEST-EH-18-007: Attempt primary return without revalidation/new authority: blocked; safety override remains available even during dwell period.

contain_critical_continuity(
  event_ref,
  containment_contract_ref,
  current_physical_state,
  assurance_profile
) -> SafeControlHandoffReceipt

Required priority:
  AGENCY/AUTHORITY REVOCATION → INDEPENDENT SAFE CONTROL HANDOFF → MINIMUM SAFE CONTINUITY → QUALIFIED RECOVERY.
The function first revokes/fences suspect authority and actuation capability at independent enforcement points. It then
uses only a separately qualified fallback controller whose current execution does not depend on the suspect AI's
mutable cognition, goals, credentials or authority. Minimum continuity and shutdown are compared using the exact domain
safety case. Determinism alone, shared training lineage, nominally separate credentials or majority agreement cannot
establish safety/independence. Recovery requires root-cause closure, repair, revalidation and fresh authorization.
